scope: Medium layout comparison, sampled mechanical screens and free-base standing/crouch-rise trials.
design_goal: Longer, lower medium layout; crouch-to-stand first, fall recovery remains a design goal.

coverage.distance_fallback: Positive convex support-plane gaps certify lower bounds when native distances conflict.
coverage.sampling: Deterministic Cartesian groups; unsampled joints reset to home for each group.

crouch_to_stand.scope: Free-base rise from a prescribed symmetric crouch; not recovery after a fall.
limitations: Only the prescribed crouch is initialized; entering it from standing or a fall is not tested.
Ideal position drives omit measured torque-speed, thermal, electrical and transmission behavior.
Ground contact uses simulation proxies and assigned masses, not qualified physical hardware.

leg_motor_location_screen.scope: Symmetric two-foot quasi-static gravity balance; no transmission or recovery validation.
assumptions: Both soles are horizontal; each foot supplies half the body weight vertically, with sagittal center of pressure at the scenario's whole-body center of mass and lateral position at sole center.
The crouch uses hip and ankle pitch offsets of minus half the knee angle. The torso stays upright.
The alternative moves knee/ankle motor mass to torso-local points (0.015, +/-0.060, 0.040)m; coincident motors are abstract mass locations, not a packaged or clearance-checked mechanism.
The alternative assumes zero transmission mass, losses, compliance or backlash and unchanged joint torque caps. Required output torque still has to pass through a real transmission.
There is no acceleration, friction, thermal model or ground-contact solver. Infeasible support checks remain failures; this calculation does not demonstrate standing up or recovery after a fall.

fall_recovery.reason: No prone, supine or side-fall recovery trajectory or qualified load-bearing contact design.

limitations: Crouch-to-stand begins from a constructed upright, flat-foot pose; it is not recovery from the floor.
Position drives are ideal torque-limited PD controls, without calibrated latency, backlash or heating.
The remote-motor comparison moves mass only and adds no transmission mass or losses; it is not a design.
Proxy-clearance improvements and successful rollouts do not qualify fabrication, walking or hardware.
